name: Certolizumab pegol
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 2 or 4 weeks after loading doses

discovery.note: Humanised Fab' fragment against TNF-α conjugated to a 40 kDa polyethylene glycol to prolong half-life. Year of first patent filing (priority June 2000, Celltech, WO 01/94585).

tagline: PEGylated anti-TNF Fab' fragment without an Fc, with minimal placental transfer
summary: Certolizumab pegol is a TNF inhibitor consisting of a humanised antibody Fab' fragment attached to polyethylene glycol. Lacking an Fc region, it does not cause complement- or antibody-mediated cytotoxicity and crosses the placenta very little; it is used in Crohn's disease, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, axial spondyloarthritis and psoriasis.
mechanism: Certolizumab binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF-α and neutralises its activity, reducing inflammatory signalling in joints, skin and gut.
The PEG moiety extends its half-life to about two weeks. Without an Fc it does not engage the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), which normally transports IgG across the placenta and into breast milk.
uses: Ankylosing spondylitis and non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis

history.title: UCB acquires Celltech
history.detail: UCB buys Celltech and the CDP870 programme.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in April for Crohn's disease.

history.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
history.detail: Approved for RA in the US and in the EU.

history.title: Spondyloarthritis and PsA
history.detail: Approved for psoriatic arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

history.title: Pregnancy data and psoriasis
history.detail: Label updated with CRIB and CRADLE data showing minimal placental and breast-milk transfer; approved for plaque psoriasis.

pk.metabolism: Proteolysis of Fab'; PEG removed largely renally

safety.boxed_warning: Serious infections (including tuberculosis, invasive fungal and opportunistic infections) and malignancy, including lymphoma.

facts: Studies (CRIB) found negligible certolizumab levels in infants of treated mothers, making it a preferred TNF inhibitor in pregnancy.
It is the only approved PEGylated TNF inhibitor.
